title: Sat3DGen: Comprehensive Street-Level 3D Scene Generation from Single Satellite Image
claim: Prior methods cover only some desired properties or give distorted results; ours satisfies all of them with higher-quality outputs and supports many downstream applications.
layout: 3 stacked bands: checkmark table, 5-column visual comparison, 4-column applications strip
description: The figure has three horizontal bands. The top band is a feature-comparison table. Its rows are Sat2City, Sat2Scene, Sat2Density++ and Ours. Its columns are Image Renderable, Satellite Faithful, More than Buildings, Supervision Signal, Synthetic or Real, and Geometry Quality. Red crosses and green checkmarks fill the cells, and the Ours row is all green checks. The middle band is a row of 3D renderings labelled (a) Sat2Scene, (b) Sat2City, the input satellite image, (c) Sat2Density++ and (d) Ours. The Sat2Scene and Sat2City renders look like building shells, Sat2Density++ looks distorted, and Ours looks cleaner. A caption below reads 'Comparison of single satellite input to 3D scene methods'. The bottom band shows four application examples: surround-view panorama video generation, satellite-to-DSM, semantic-map-to-3D, and large-area mesh generation. The eye goes first to the red and green marks in the table, then to the renders.
caption: Comparison of 3D scene generation methods (top: attribute table; bottom: visual results). Given an input satellite image, (a) Sat2Scene and (b) Sat2City generate only shells of buildings and roads and miss non‑building semantics; (c) Sat2Density++ and (d) Ours are faithful to satellite semantics and appearance, but Sat2Density++ is heavily distorted, whereas our Sat3DGen yields a more structured, higher‑quality 3D representation.
abstract: Generating a street-level 3D scene from a single satellite image is a crucial yet challenging task. Current methods present a stark trade-off: geometry-colorization models achieve high geometric fidelity but are typically building-focused and lack semantic diversity. In contrast, proxy-based models use feed-forward image-to-3D frameworks to generate holistic scenes by jointly learning geometry and texture, a process that yields rich content but coarse and unstable geometry. We attribute these geometric failures to the extreme viewpoint gap and sparse, inconsistent supervision inherent in satellite-to-street data. We introduce Sat3DGen to address these fundamental challenges, which embodies a geometry-first methodology. This methodology enhances the feed-forward paradigm by integrating novel geometric constraints with a perspective-view training strategy, explicitly countering the primary sources of geometric error. This geometry-centric strategy yields a dramatic leap in both 3D accuracy and photorealism. For validation, we first constructed a new benchmark by pairing the VIGOR-OOD test set with high-resolution DSM data. On this benchmark, our method improves geometric RMSE from 6.76m to 5.20m. Crucially, this geometric leap also boosts photorealism, reducing the FrÃ©chet Inception Distance (FID) from $\sim$40 to 19 against the leading method, Sat2Density++, despite using no extra tailored image-quality modules. We demonstrate the versatility of our high-quality 3D assets through diverse downstream applications, including semantic-map-to-3D synthesis, multi-camera video generation, large-scale meshing, and unsupervised single-image Digital Surface Model (DSM) estimation. The code has been released on https://github.com/qianmingduowan/Sat3DGen.
